TABATABAI:36:66-83/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r6.speaker: أبي بن خلف
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r6.claim: Al-Ayyashi transmits from al-Sadiq that Ubayy ibn Khalaf crumbled a decayed bone and challenged the resurrection; God answered that the one who first created it will revive it.
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r6.anchor: عن الحلبي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال جاء أبي بن خلف فأخذ عظما باليا من حائط ففته

TABATABAI:36:66-83/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وعروة بن الزبير وقتادة والسدي وعكرمة
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r7.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthur gives many routes for a similar report, while other reports from Ibn Abbas name al-As ibn Wa'il or Abd Allah ibn Ubayy as the challenger.
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r7.anchor: وروى مثله في الدر المنثور بطرق كثيرة عن ابن عباس وعروة بن الزبير وعن قتادة والسدي وعكرمة

TABATABAI:36:66-83/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r8.claim: Al-Tabataba'i notes the alternate attributions of the bone challenge to al-As ibn Wa'il and Abd Allah ibn Ubayy in other Ibn Abbas reports.
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r8.anchor: وروى أيضا عن ابن عباس أن القائل هو العاص بن وائل وبطريق آخر عنه أن القائل هو عبد الله بن أبي

TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r1.claim: The one who originated a person from nothing and without a prior model can restore that person as originally created.
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r1.anchor:
قال صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
" إن الذي أنشأه من غير شيء وصوره على غير مثال كان سبق إليه قادر أن يعيده كما بدأه

TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r2.claim: Souls remain in their stations; bodily remains are preserved in earth and reassembled after the resurrection rain, then reunited with each soul.
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r2.anchor: إن الروح مقيمة في مكانها روح المحسن في ضياء وفسحة، وروح المسيء في ضيق وظلمة

TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r3.speaker: نهج البلاغة
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r3.claim: God's creative command is an effective act, not an audible sound; if it were eternal, that would imply a second deity.
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r3.anchor: لما أراد كونه كن فيكون، لا بصوت يقرع ولا نداء يسمع وإنما كلامه سبحانه فعل منه أنشأه

TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r4.speaker: أبو الحسن عليه السلام
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r4.claim: Safwan reports that human will is inward intention followed by action, while God's will is simply bringing something into existence.
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r4.anchor: الإرادة من الخلق الضمير وما يبدو لهم بعد ذلك من الفعل، وأما من الله فإرادته إحداثه لا غير ذلك

TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r5.claim: The Imams' reports are numerous in treating divine will as an attribute of action rather than an inward creaturely state.
TABATABAI:36:66-83#2/r5.anchor: والروايات عنهم عليه السلام في كون إرادته من صفات الفعل مستفيضة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r6.claim: The closing section resumes the opening themes of monotheism and the Hereafter and assures the Prophet that he awakens the morally living, not the dead-hearted.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r6.anchor: what was discussed in the opening one is take up again in a different style

STUDYQURAN:36:78/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:78/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:36:78/r1.claim: These verses voice a common objection to the Qur'anic teaching of bodily resurrection, also raised elsewhere in the Qur'an.
STUDYQURAN:36:78/r1.anchor: These verses express a common objection to the Quranic understanding of bodily resurrection (cf. 13:5; 17:49, 98; 23:35, 82–83; 27:67;

STUDYQURAN:36:78/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:78/r2.speaker: IK, JJ, Q, W
STUDYQURAN:36:78/r2.claim: A report says Ubayy ibn Khalaf brought the Prophet withered bones, crushed them, and challenged their revival; the Prophet affirmed it and warned that Ubayy would be cast into the Fire, after which these verses were revealed.
STUDYQURAN:36:78/r2.anchor: it is reported that a man by the name of Ubayy ibn Khalaf brought some withered bones to the Prophet and crushed them into pieces

STUDYQURAN:36:78/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:78/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:36:78/r4.claim: Verse 79 has a similar passage at 17:51.
STUDYQURAN:36:78/r4.anchor: For a passage similar to v. 79, see 17:51.

BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r1.claim: Muhammad is told to shame the denier by recalling the natural constitution he forgot and directing him to infer from it.
BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r1.anchor: تبكيتا لذلك الإنسان المنكر بتذكير ما نسيه من فطرة الدالة على حقيقة الحال وإرشاده الطريقة للاستشهاد بها

BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r2.claim: The one who first brought the bones into existence from nothing will revive them; the argument from initial creation to return is decisive proof of bodily resurrection and refutes its deniers.
BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r2.anchor: أي : في أول مرة ولم تكن شيئا فإن قدرته كما هي لاستحالة التغير فيها

BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r3.claim: God knows every detail of creation and its re-creation, including every scattered particle and its original and derivative parts and how they are joined, separated, gathered, or dispersed, and restores each in its prior pattern and powers.
BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r3.anchor: مبالغ في العلم بتفاصيل كيفيات الخلق والإيجاد إنشاء وإعادة محيط بجميع الأجزاء المتفتتة المتبددة لكل شخص من الأشخاص

BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r4.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r4.claim: Al-Bahr al-ulum says God gathers each person's original particles, restores their souls, and raises bodies and souls as they were.
BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r4.anchor: وفي "بحر العلوم" بليغ العلم بكل شيء من المخلوقات لا يخفى عليه شيء من الأجزاء المتفتتة

BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r5.speaker: القاضي عضد الدين
BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r5.claim: In al-Mawaqif, Qadi ʿAdud al-Din leaves undecided whether God annihilates bodily particles then recreates them or disperses and recomposes them, because neither option has proof.
BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r5.anchor: قال القاضي عضد الدين في "المواقف" هل يعدم الله الأجزاء البدنية

BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r6.claim: The cited verse “Everything perishes except His face” does not decide between the two accounts, since destruction can mean annihilating parts or dispersing them and eliminating their functions.
BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r6.anchor: وقوله تعالى : {كل شيء هالك إلا وجهه} لا يرجح أحد الاحتمالين

BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r7.claim: The resurrected body is numerically the same as the original through its individuating accidents, whether God restores annihilated original parts and qualities or recombines dispersed parts and recreates life.
BURSEVI:v7p342#2/r7.anchor: فالجسم المعاد هو المبتدأ بعينه أي : بجميع عوارضه المشخصة

BURSEVI:v7p343/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p343/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p343/r1.claim: Most deniers offer no proof and rely on sheer improbability, as in their questions about being raised after becoming dust or bones.
BURSEVI:v7p343/r1.anchor: واعلم أن المنكرين للحشر منهم من لم يذكر فيه دليلا ولا شبهة بل اكتفى بمجرد الاستبعاد

BURSEVI:v7p343/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p343/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p343/r2.claim: God rebuts their incredulity by recalling that He first formed humans from dust and semen, fashioned diverse organs, and gave them speech and intellect, the grounds of their honor.
BURSEVI:v7p343/r2.anchor: نسي أنا خلقناه من تراب ثم من نطفة متشابهة الأجزاء ثم جعلنا له من ناصيته إلى قدمه أعضاء مختلفة الصور

BURSEVI:v7p343/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p343/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p343/r3.claim: If deniers find original creation of a speaking, reasoning person from a filthy, lifeless drop plausible, they have no basis to find restoration implausible.
BURSEVI:v7p343/r3.anchor: فإن كانوا يقنعون بمجرد الاستبعاد فهلا يستبعدون خلق الناطق العاقل من نطفة قذرة لم تكن محلا للحياة أصلا

BURSEVI:v7p343/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p343/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p343/r4.claim: One objection says that after annihilation nothing remains, so existence cannot be predicated of what is nonexistent; God answers that He can restore people as He first created them when they were unremembered.
BURSEVI:v7p343/r4.anchor: أنه بعد العدم لم يبق شيئا فكيف يصح على العدم الحكم بالوجود فأجاب تعالى عن هذه الشبهة

BURSEVI:v7p343/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p343/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p343/r5.claim: A second objection asks how dispersed bodily parts, including parts eaten by animals or incorporated into another person's body, can be reunited without depriving either person of a body.
BURSEVI:v7p343/r5.anchor: أن من تفرقت أجزاؤه في مشارق العالم ومغاربه وصار بعضه في أبدان السباع وبعضه في حواصل الطيور

BURSEVI:v7p343/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p343/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p343/r6.claim: God's complete knowledge of every creation refutes the difficulty of distinguishing the dispersed parts needed for resurrection.
BURSEVI:v7p343/r6.anchor: فأبطل الله هذه الشبهة بقوله : {وهو بكل خلق عليم}

BURSEVI:v7p343#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p343#2/r1.speaker: بعض الأفاضل
BURSEVI:v7p343#2/r1.claim: A learned authority frames the problem as both intermingled body parts and the dryness of decayed bones, since life requires bodily moisture.
BURSEVI:v7p343#2/r1.anchor: قال بعض الأفاضل : لما كان تمسكهم بكون العظام رميمة من وجهين : أحدهما : اختلاط أجزاء الأبدان

BURSEVI:v7p343#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p343#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p343#2/r2.claim: God's knowledge enables Him to distinguish the parts of different bodies, answering the first difficulty.
BURSEVI:v7p343#2/r2.anchor: أشار إلى جواب الأول بقوله : {وهو بكل خلق عليم} فيمكنه تمييز أجزاء الأبدان

BURSEVI:v7p343#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p343#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p343#2/r10.claim: People readily accept fire from green wood, so they should accept resurrection; producing fire from watery wood shows God's power to unite opposites and restore what dried out.
BURSEVI:v7p343#2/r10.anchor: كذلك لا تشكون في أن الله يحيي الموتى ويخرجهم من القبور للسؤال والجزاء

TAB-FULL:v19p486/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p486/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p486/r6.claim: The answer identifies the one who first originated the bones as the one who will revive them, and says He knows every creation.
TAB-FULL:v19p486/r6.anchor: فقال الله: {قل يحييها الذي أنشأها أول مرة وهو بكل خلق عليم} [يس: 79]

TAB-FULL:v19p488/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p488/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p488/r3.claim: The one who revives the bones is the one who first brought them into being when they were nothing.
TAB-FULL:v19p488/r3.anchor: يحييها الذي ابتدع خلقها أول مرة ولم تكن شيئا

TAB-FULL:v19p488/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p488/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p488/r4.claim: God knows every creature and how to cause death, revive, originate, and restore; nothing about His creation is hidden.
TAB-FULL:v19p488/r4.anchor: وهو بجميع خلقه ذو علم كيف يميت، وكيف يحيي،

TABATABAI:36:76-80/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:76-80/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:76-80/r10.claim: The challenger forgets his first creation from a sperm drop; if he remembered it, he could answer his own challenge by recalling that initial creation, as God instructs the Prophet to do.
TABATABAI:36:76-80/r10.anchor: وضرب الإنسان لنا مثلا وقد نسي خلقه من نطفة لأول مرة

TABATABAI:36:76-80/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:76-80/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:76-80/r11.claim: God teaches the Prophet to answer that the one who brought the bones into being the first time will revive them; أول مرة reinforces the initial creation.
TABATABAI:36:76-80/r11.anchor: الإنشاء هو الإيجاد الابتدائي وتقييده بقوله { أول مرة } للتأكيد

TABATABAI:36:76-80/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:76-80/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:76-80/r12.claim: God knows every creation and does not forget what the bones were before and after death; His power and knowledge make their revival possible.
TABATABAI:36:76-80/r12.anchor: فإذا كان هو خالق هذه العظام لأول مرة وهو لا يجهل شيئا مما كانت عليه قبل الموت وبعده فإحياؤه ثانيا بمكان من الإمكان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p527/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p527/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p527/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses God's creating it the first time as originating it initially.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p527/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد ابتدأها أول مرة (¬5).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p527/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p527/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p527/r2.claim: Abu Ishaq argues that God's power is more evident in originating creation than in recreating it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p527/r2.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: والقدرة في الإبتداء أبين من الإعادة (¬6).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p527/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p527/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p527/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says God knows creation both when He first originates it and when He revives it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p527/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد حين ابتدأه وحين يعيده (¬7).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p527/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p527/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p527/r4.claim: Muqatil says God knows their creation in worldly life and their creation after death.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p527/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل: عليهم بخلقهم في الدنيا وعليم بخلقهم بعد الموت (¬8).

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:79-83/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:79-83/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:79-83/r1.claim: The One who created the bones initially can revive them, and He knows every creation, both its beginning and its return.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:79-83/r1.anchor: خلقها { أول مرة وهو بكل خلق } من الابتداء والإعادة { عليم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p820/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p820/r9.speaker: يحيى
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p820/r9.claim: Yaḥyā says he heard that the Prophet answered that God would revive Ubayy after death and then put him in the Fire; the verse was then revealed.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p820/r9.anchor: قال يحيى: فبلغني أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال له: «يحييك الله بعد موتك ثم يدخلك النار»

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p820/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p820/r10.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p820/r10.claim: The one who originated the bones can revive them and knows every creation, as in 67:14's question about whether the Creator knows what He created.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p820/r10.anchor: كقوله: {ألا يعلم من خلق} [الملك: 14] ، أي: بلى

ELMALILI:36:77-83/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:77-83/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:77-83/r2.claim: God knows every creature's details, including all its gathered and scattered parts, roots, branches, conditions, qualities, quantities, and particular features.
ELMALILI:36:77-83/r2.anchor: her mahlûku bütün tafsîlâtıyla, her birinin toplanan ve dağılan bütün eczâsı, usûl ü fürû‘u, evzâ‘ı, ahvâli, keyfiyyât ve kemmiyyâtı

ELMALILI:36:77-83/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:77-83/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:77-83/r3.claim: He knows every mode and kind of creation, whether material or immaterial, with or without means or precedent, whether first or later.
ELMALILI:36:77-83/r3.anchor: her halkı, yaratmanın her türlüsünü bilir; maddeli maddesiz, âletli âletsiz, örnekli örneksiz, gerek ilkin gerek sonra her nev‘ini bilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r1.claim: The passage exposes the contradiction of someone who neglects reflection on his own creation, then arrogantly judges the Creator's and Prophet's statements using reason alone.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r1.anchor: İnsanın kendi yaratılışı üzerinde düşünmeyi bir kenara bırakıp, küstahça bir tavırla yüce yaratıcının ve peygamberinin bildirdiklerini yalnızca aklıyla

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r6.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r6.claim: In the report, the Prophet replies that God will kill the challenger, resurrect him, and cast him into Hell.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r6.anchor: Resûl-i Ekrem de “Evet. Nitekim O seni de öldürecek, sonra diriltip cehenneme atacak!” cevabını verir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r10.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r10.claim: Razi says the general meaning matters more than the specific occasion: the passage condemns denial of God's power and resurrection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r10.anchor: Râzî’nin belirttiği üzere önemli olan, özel sebep ne olursa olsun sözün genelinden çıkan mânadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r11.claim: Khalq at the verse's end can mean both “creating” and “created beings,” so the statement encompasses both senses.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r11.anchor: 79. âyetin son cümlesinde geçen halk kelimesi hem “yaratma” hem “yaratılanlar” (mahlûkat) anlamına geldiği için

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r12.claim: God knows every creature in all its details and every kind of creation, whether material or immaterial, with or without instruments or models, initially or later.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:77/r12.anchor: Allah Teâlâ, yaratılanların hepsini bütün ayrıntılarıyla, her birini toplanan ve dağılan parçalarıyla, usulü ve fürûu, içinde bulunduğu durumları, nitelik ve nicelikleri, her türlü özellikleriyle bilir

BURHAN:v4p47/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p47/r2.speaker: ابن مالك
BURHAN:v4p47/r2.claim: Answers normally match the question’s clause type, but Ibn Mālik analyzes a short answer such as ‘Zayd’ to ‘Who read?’ as a verbal clause with its verb omitted; complete answers retain the verb, as in the resurrection exchange.
BURHAN:v4p47/r2.anchor: قال وإنما قدرته كذلك لا مبتدأ مع احتماله

BURHAN:v4p47/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p47/r5.speaker: شهاب الدين بن المرحل
BURHAN:v4p47/r5.claim: Ibn al-Muraḥḥal treats these replies as answering with wording different from the question for a rhetorical point, like the answer about lunar phases; the author says this analysis is questionable.
BURHAN:v4p47/r5.anchor: فكان الشيخ شهاب الدين بن المرحل رحمه الله يجعله من باب

BURHAN:v4p47/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p47/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p47/r6.claim: A short answer like ‘Zayd’ explicitly signals that it answers ‘Who came?’; unlike ‘Zayd came,’ it cannot also stand as an unrelated sentence and conveys the restriction ‘the one who came was Zayd.’
BURHAN:v4p47/r6.anchor: ولو قلت زيد كان نصا في أنه جواب وفي العموم الذي دلت عليه من وكأنك قلت الذي جاء زيد فيفيد الحصر

BURHAN:v2p25/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p25/r3.speaker: أبي بن خلف
BURHAN:v2p25/r3.claim: Ubayy ibn Khalaf reportedly brought decayed bones, crumbled and scattered them, and challenged Muhammad over who could revive them; the answer points to the first creation and God’s knowledge of every creation.

BURHAN:v2p25/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p25/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p25/r4.claim: The reply argues from the first creation to resurrection by their shared coming-to-be, then strengthens the case by noting that God brings fire from green trees through changed properties.
BURHAN:v2p25/r4.anchor: وهذا فى غاية البيان فى رد الشيء إلى نظيره والجمع بينهما من حيث تبديل الأعراض عليهما

BURHAN:v1p402/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p402/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p402/r1.claim: The yāʾ is omitted from standalone يحيى but retained with its object pronoun: inner life is clearer to knowledge and stronger in perception than outward life.
BURHAN:v1p402/r1.anchor: لأن حياة الباطن أظهر فى العلم من حياة الظاهر وأقوى فى الإدراك

BURHAN:v1p402/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p402/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p402/r3.claim: More generally, omitted yāʾ can signal absence from perception and connection to submission to God in the station of excellence.
BURHAN:v1p402/r3.anchor: الضرب الثانى الذى تسقط فيه الياء فى الخط والتلاوة فهو اعتبار غيبة عن باب الإدراك جملة واتصاله بالإسلام لله

BURHAN:v4p48/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p48/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p48/r1.claim: Question-and-answer passages often omit what the question supplies, but the answer here explicitly says “revives” to spell out the resurrection they denied.
BURHAN:v4p48/r1.anchor: ولعله للتنصيص على الإحياء الذي أنكروه

BURHAN:v3p228/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p228/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p228/r1.claim: The exchange about reviving bones after the denier forgets his own creation is described as the strongest form of argument.
BURHAN:v3p228/r1.anchor: وهذا أشد ما يكون من الحجاج

BURHAN:v3p467/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p467/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p467/r6.claim: The reply argues that the one who originated the bones the first time can revive them.
BURHAN:v3p467/r6.anchor: قل يحييها الذي أنشأها أول مرة

ITQAN:v2p575#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p575#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p575#3/r1.claim: Answers generally match the question's sentence form; the verbal answers in 5:4 and 36:79 show that an omitted verb should be estimated before the stated answer.

ITQAN:v4p357/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p357/r3.speaker: أبي بن خلف
ITQAN:v4p357/r3.claim: Al-Hakim and others report that Ubayy ibn Khalaf crumbled a bone and challenged whether God could revive it; the verse answered by pointing to first creation.
ITQAN:v4p357/r3.anchor: أن أبي بن خلف جاء بعظم ففته فقال

ITQAN:v4p357/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p357/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p357/r4.claim: The argument returns the second creation to the first through their shared origin, then adds the vivid parallel of fire coming from green wood, which undergoes changing qualities.
ITQAN:v4p357/r4.anchor: فاستدل سبحانه وتعالى برد النشأة الأخرى إلى الأولى والجمع بينهما بعلة الحدوث

RUMMANI:v1p106/r11.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p106/r11.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p106/r11.claim: The reply to the denier who forgets his own creation—that the one who created the bones initially will revive them and knows every creation—is singled out as supremely persuasive.
RUMMANI:v1p106/r11.anchor: وضرب لنا مثلا ونسي خلقه قال من يحيي العظام وهي رميم قل يحييها الذي أنشأها أول مرة وهو بكل خلق عليم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p280/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p280/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p280/r1.claim: Anā can mean “how,” as in the question about how God will revive the town and the instruction to approach the field as one wishes.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p280/r1.anchor: أني: يكون بمعنيين. يكون بمعنى: كيف

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p280/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p280/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p280/r2.claim: Anā can also mean “from where,” as in the questions about the source of God's child and how disbelievers are turned away.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p280/r2.anchor: وتكون بمعنى: من أين، نحو قوله

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p280/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p280/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p280/r3.claim: The two senses are close enough that either may be interpreted through the other; al-Kumayt's line explicitly uses both “anā” and “min ayna.”
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p280/r3.anchor: وقال الكميت : أنى ومن أين آبك الطرب

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p416/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p416/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p416/r1.claim: The one who gave people life the first time will resurrect them; if their first creation was no burden for God, re-creation cannot be burdensome.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p416/r1.anchor: the one who gave them life the first time will raise them to life again.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p416/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p416/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p416/r3.claim: Here khalq means creatures: God is aware of all His creatures.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p416/r3.anchor: In other words, God is aware of all His creatures.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p416/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p416/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p416/r4.claim: God’s knowledge includes every part of people’s bodies, even after death: 67:14 says the Creator knows what He made, and 50:4 says what earth consumes is recorded with Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p416/r4.anchor: He is aware of every bit and part of their body.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r9.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says the phrase ‘He revives them’ plainly supports the view that life enters the bones.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r9.anchor: واستدل بقوله: قل يحييها على أن الحياة تحلها، وهذا الاستدلال ظاهر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r10.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r10.claim: Those who deny that life inhabits bones interpret their revival as restoring them to fresh, moist form in a sound, perceptive body.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r10.anchor: ومن قال: إن الحياة لا تحلها، قال: المراد بإحياء العظام: ردها إلى ما كانت عليه غضة رطبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r11.claim: God knows every manner of creation, and nothing created, fine or immense and of any kind, is beyond His power.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p84/r11.anchor: وهو بكل خلق عليم: يعلم كيفيات ما يخلق، لا يتعاظمه شيء من المنشآت والمعدات جنسا ونوعا

ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r1.claim: The command rebukes the objector by recalling evidence in his nature and directing him to reason from it.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r1.anchor: تبكيتا له بتذكير ما نسيه من فطرته الدالة على حقيقة الحال

ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r2.claim: The One who first brought the bones into being and developed them will revive them; re-creation is easier than originating them without precedent.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r2.anchor: إذ لم يسبق لها إيجاد ولا شك أن الإحياء بعد أهون من الإنشاء قبل

ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r3.claim: No incapacity can arise in God, since His power is essential and eternal and cannot cease or change.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r3.anchor: ولا احتمال لعروض العجز فإن قدرته عز وجل ذاتية أزلية لا تقبل الزوال ولا التغير

ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r4.speaker: الفارابي
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r4.claim: Al-Farabi wished Aristotle had seen the syllogism: whoever first creates can recreate and revive; God first created and animated the bones, so He can restore them with their powers.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r4.anchor: كان الفارابي يقول وددت لو أن أرسطو وقف على القياس الجلي في قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r5.claim: The verse appears to support the Shafi'i position, also attributed to Malik and Ahmad, that bones receive life and undergo death; carrion bones are then impure.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r5.anchor: والآية ظاهرة فيما ذهب إليه الإمام الشافعي قيل ومالك وأحمد من أن العظم تحله الحياة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r6.claim: Whether bones receive life is disputed among jurists and philosophers; proponents of no life argue that life entails sensation while bones feel no pain when cut.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r6.anchor: مما اختلف فيه الفقهاء والحكماء واستدل من قال منها بعدم حلولها فيه بأن الحياة تستلزم الحس

ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r7.speaker: إبن زهر
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r7.claim: Ibn Zuhr says Galen's remarks on bone sensation are inconsistent, and concludes bones have slow sensation because animal spirit prevents their decay during life.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r7.anchor: ابن زهر في كتاب التيسير : اضطرب كلام جالينوس في العظام هل لها إحساس

ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r8.claim: Some jurists say bones have no life and stay pure after death; they read bones as their owner or revival as restoring them to living moist form, but al-Alusi says those readings depart from the apparent sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r8.anchor: فحيث لم تحلها الحياة لم يحلها الموت فلم تكن نجسة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r9.claim: Other jurists accept the verse as evidence bones have life but still regard them as pure, because carrion impurity comes from moisture and flowing blood, which bones lack.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p54#2/r9.anchor: ومن الفقهاء القائلين بعدم نجاسة عظام الميتة من رأى قوة الإستدلال بالآية

ALUSI-FULL:v23p55/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p55/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p55/r1.claim: God knows every created thing, including each person's scattered fragments and how parts were connected, separated, gathered, or dispersed.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p55/r1.anchor: مبالغ في العلم فيعلم جل وعلا بجميع الأجزاء المتفتتة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p55/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p55/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p55/r2.claim: God restores each person's parts to their former arrangement and powers; the closing clause either confirms the argument or joins the relative clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p55/r2.anchor: فيعيد كلا من ذلك على النمط السابق مع القوى التي كانت قبل والجملة إما اعتراض تذييلي

ALUSI-FULL:v23p55/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p55/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p55/r3.claim: The nominal sentence signals that God's knowledge is continuous, unlike His acts of creating particular things.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p55/r3.anchor: والعدول إلى الإسمية للتنبيه على أن علمه تعالى بما ذكر أمر مستمر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p29/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p29/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p29/r4.claim: The One who first brought the bones into being is the One who will revive them; “created” explains “brought into being.”

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:78-79/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:78-79/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:78-79/r5.claim: The one who originated the bones the first time will revive them; God's capacity has not changed, and the underlying matter remains receptive by its nature.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:78-79/r5.anchor: فإن قدرته كما كانت لامتناع التغير فيه والمادة على حالها

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:78-79/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:78-79/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:78-79/r6.claim: God knows every created thing in detail, including the origins, divisions, locations, and means of identifying scattered fragments, and how to reassemble them as before and restore their qualities or equivalents.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:78-79/r6.anchor: يعلم تفاصيل المخلوقات بعلمه وكيفية خلقها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r1.claim: Because listeners await a reply to the objection, the command to speak begins the answer and addresses the person able to understand the dispute fully.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r1.anchor: ولما كان موطنا يتشوف فيه السامع لهذا الكلام إلى جوابه , استأنف قوله مخاطبا من لا يفهم هذه المجادلة حق فهمها غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r2.claim: The answer repeats the verb 'revive' explicitly to prevent evasive argument and to stress the intended point.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r2.anchor: وأعاد فعل الإحياء نصا على المراد دفعا للتعنت ودلالة على الاهتمام

BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r3.claim: The One who originated the bones from nothing and gave them life the first time can restore them a second time; original creation proves the ability to recreate.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r3.anchor: أي فإن كل من قدر على إيجاد شيء أول مرة فهو قادر على إعادته ثاني مرة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r4.claim: Because life can enter bone, bone becomes impure at death; the verse therefore supports the ruling that a dead animal's bones are impure.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r4.anchor: وهي شاهدة بأن الحياة تحل العظم فيتنجس بالموت مما يحكم بنجاسة ميتته

BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r5.claim: Khalq here means every possible act of making and measuring, whether bringing something into being initially or recreating it.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r5.anchor: أي صنع وتقدير ممكن أن يخلق من ذلك ومن غيره ابتداء وإعادة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r6.claim: God knows every particle of a dead person even if scattered across land and sea, as well as everything else.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r6.anchor: فلا يخفى عليه أجراء ميت أصلا وإن تفرقت في البر والبحر

BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r7.claim: This is a case of badīʿ al-iḥtibāk: first resurrection points to the second, second origination to the first, and 'first time' implies a second time.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r7.anchor: فالآية من بديع الاحتباك : الإحياء أولا دال على مثله ثانيا , والإنشاء ثانيا دال على مثله أولا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r8.claim: The proof completes the surah's prior descriptions of resurrection, gathering, judgment, and the afterlife, together establishing bodily and spiritual resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p285/r8.anchor: فقد بلغ هذا البيان في الدلالة على البعث الجسماني والروحاني معا النهاية التي ليش وراءها بيان

DURR-FULL:v7p74/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p74/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p74/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Ubayy ibn Khalaf brought a withered bone, broke it, and challenged how God could revive it; the Prophet answered that God would revive it, kill Ubayy, and admit him to Hell.
DURR-FULL:v7p74/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: جاء أبي بن خلف وفي يده عظم حائل

DURR-FULL:v7p74/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p74/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p74/r2.claim: In another account, Ubayy al-Jumahi crumbled a rotten bone and scattered it in the wind; the Prophet said God would revive it, kill Ubayy, and put him in Hell.
DURR-FULL:v7p74/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: جاء أبي بن خلف الجمحي إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعظم نخر

DURR-FULL:v7p74/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p74/r3.speaker: أبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v7p74/r3.claim: Abu Malik says Ubayy asked who would revive the bones, and God revealed the passage beginning with man's creation from a drop and ending with God's knowledge of every thing.
DURR-FULL:v7p74/r3.anchor: عن أبي مالك قال: جاء أبي بن خلف بعظم نخرة فجعل يفته بين يدي النبي

DURR-FULL:v7p74/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p74/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p74/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that this verse was revealed about Abu Jahl, who crumbled a withered bone and asked who could revive it.
DURR-FULL:v7p74/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: نزلت هذه الآية في أبي جهل بن هشام جاء بعظم

DURR-FULL:v7p74/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p74/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p74/r5.claim: Mujahid identifies the man who brought the bone as Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who challenged the Prophet about resurrection while crumbling it.
DURR-FULL:v7p74/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {وضرب لنا مثلا} قال: أبي بن خلف جاء بعظم

DURR-FULL:v7p74/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p74/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p74/r6.claim: Qatada says the challenge was revealed about Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who scattered a rotten bone in the wind; the Prophet answered that God would revive it and send him to the Fire.
DURR-FULL:v7p74/r6.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {وضرب لنا مثلا} قال: نزلت في أبي بن خلف جاء بعظم نخر

DURR-FULL:v7p75/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p75/r2.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v7p75/r2.claim: Ikrima reports that when Ubayy asked who would revive the bone, the Prophet replied that creating it before it existed was more wondrous than reviving it after it had existed.
DURR-FULL:v7p75/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه قال: جاء أبي بن خلف إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وفي يده عظم حائل

DURR-FULL:v7p75/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p75/r3.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v7p75/r3.claim: Urwa says the resurrection announcement was vehemently denied; Ubayy crumbled and scattered a bone, provoking the Prophet, and God then revealed this answer.
DURR-FULL:v7p75/r3.anchor: عن عروة بن الزبير رضي الله عنه قال: لما أنزل الله على رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الناس يحاسبون بأعمالهم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3203/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3203/r1.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3203/r1.claim: ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr reports that after people vehemently denied resurrection, Ubayy ibn Khalaf crumbled a rotten bone into the wind and challenged the Prophet; the Prophet was deeply hurt, and God revealed that its first creator would revive it.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3203/r1.anchor: عروة بن الزبير رضي الله ، عنه قال : لما انزل الله على رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r7.claim: The reply establishes the proof that a person who began as a sperm can become an articulate disputant; this first creation is itself a revival after nonexistence and lack of life.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r7.anchor: ثم نزلت الآية مبينة ومقيمة للحجة في أن الإنسان نطفة ثم يكون بعد ذلك خصيما مبينا هل هذا إلا إحياء بعد موت وعدم حياة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r10.claim: God first directs people to reflect on the first creation, then adds a third proof: producing fire from green, water-filled wood.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p463#2/r10.anchor: ثم دلهم تعالى على الاعتبار بالنشأة الأولى، ثم عقب ذلك تعالى بدليل ثالث في إيجاد النار في العود الأخضر المرتوي ماء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p42/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p42/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p42/r1.claim: The one who originated the bones the first time can revive them, and He knows every act of creation, both origination and restoration.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد، وعكرمة، وعروة بن الزبير، والسدي، وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r1.claim: These authorities report that Ubayy ibn Khalaf came to Muhammad with a decayed bone, crumbled and scattered it, and challenged whether God would resurrect it; the final verses of Yasin were revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد، وعكرمة، وعروة بن الزبير، والسدي. وقتادة: جاء أبي بن خلف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report through Saʿid ibn Jubayr, says al-Asi ibn Waʾil took a bone from al-Batha, crushed it, and asked Muhammad whether God could revive it; Muhammad said God would resurrect and send him to Hell, and Yasin's closing verses were revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير (6) ، عن ابن عباس، أن العاصي (7) بن وائل أخذ عظما من البطحاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r3.claim: Ibn Jarir transmits the al-Asi ibn Waʾil report through Saʿid ibn Jubayr but does not name Ibn Abbas in its chain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r3.anchor: ورواه ابن جرير عن يعقوب بن إبراهيم، عن هشيم، عن أبي بشر، عن سعيد بن جبير، فذكره ولم يذكر "ابن عباس"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r4.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r4.claim: Al-Awfi's report names Abdullah ibn Ubayy as the visitor, but Ibn Kathir rejects it as munkar because Yasin is Meccan and Ibn Ubayy was in Medina.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p593#3/r4.anchor: وروي من طريق العوفي، عن ابن عباس قال: جاء عبد الله بن أبي بعظم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p594/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p594/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p594/r4.claim: God knows the bones throughout the earth, including where they went and how they were dispersed and fragmented.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p594/r4.anchor: أي: يعلم العظام في سائر أقطار الأرض وأرجائها، أين ذهبت، وأين تفرقت وتمزقت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p594/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p594/r5.speaker: حذيفة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p594/r5.claim: Ahmad reports Hudhayfa's account of a dying man who ordered his family to burn and scatter his remains; God reassembled and questioned him, then forgave him for fearing God. Uqba ibn Amr confirms hearing the Prophet tell it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p594/r5.anchor: عن ربعي قال: قال عقبة بن عمرو لحذيفة: ألا تحدثنا ما سمعت من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم؟

JISHUMI:v8p5900/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r11.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r11.claim: A polytheist brought a crumbled old bone and challenged Muhammad about God reviving it; the passage from this verse to the sūra’s end was revealed.
JISHUMI:v8p5900/r11.anchor: قيل: جاء مشرك بعظم بال متفتت، وقال: يا محمد، أتزعم أن الله يبعث هذا بعدما بلي؟ فقال: نعم، فنزلت الآية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r8.claim: God knows how to create and is not daunted by any created thing, whether its forms are great or minute.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p32#3/r8.anchor: يعلم كيف يخلق ، لا يتعاظمه شيء

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports al-As ibn Wa'il crumbling a bone and questioning resurrection; the Prophet said God would revive him, then kill and resurrect him and put him in Hell.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r2.anchor: فنزلت هذه الآيات فيه ، قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r9.claim: The one who first created them from nothing can restore them from existing matter.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r9.anchor: من قدر عل إنشائها أول مرة من غير شيء فهو قادرعلى إعادتها في النشأة الثانية من شيء

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p32#2/r10.claim: God knows how to initiate creation and restore it.

MUQATIL:36:79-80/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:79-80/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:79-80/r1.claim: Tell Ubayy that God will revive the bones at Resurrection, since He first created them from nothing in this world.
MUQATIL:36:79-80/r1.anchor: { يحييها } يوم القيامة { الذي أنشأها } خلقها { أول مرة } من الدنيا ولم تك شيئا

MUQATIL:36:79-80/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:79-80/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:79-80/r2.claim: God knows their creation in this world and their new creation after death.
MUQATIL:36:79-80/r2.anchor: عليم بخلقهم فى الدنيا عليم بخلقهم فى الآخرة بعد الموت خلقا جديدا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p15#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15#2/r1.claim: Anshaʾahā means created them, and the first time means their initial creation.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p15#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15#2/r2.claim: Here khalq means every created thing.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p15#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15#2/r3.claim: God knows every creature's parts, even dispersed across land and sea, and gathers and restores them as before.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p15#2/r3.anchor: لا تخفى عليه أجزاؤه وان تفرقت فى البر والبحر فيجمعه ويعيده كما كان

QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r7.claim: The one who originated the bones from nothing can restore them in the second creation from the remaining tailbone.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r7.anchor: أي من غير شيء فهو قادر على إعادتها في النشأة الثانية من شيء وهو عجم الذنب

QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r8.claim: The tailbone is called ʿajm al-dhanab, with an alternate spelling ʿajb using bāʾ.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:78-79/r9.claim: God knows how to originate and how to restore every creation.
